dct_description_sm: The purpose of this study was to better understand the relationship between a changing treeline and people's lives in the changing tundra-treeline region of Northern Canada, using photographs and plants to focus community-based research on changes and their impacts.  This research looks at lived experience of changes in the landscape and environment that we can see by comparing photographs taken in earlier times with what we see today.  As well, a herbarium of plants was created with each participating community to establish a baseline to track future changes in vegetation.  It broadens the range of information considered in research by inviting community members to be participants and community organizations to be research partners.  We hope that by bringing people with different kinds of knowledge and ways of understanding together to talk about changes in the environment, as we look at the changes apparent in both photographic images and in distributions of plants, that we all will learn new knowledge about the changing environment and our shared understanding of it.  We are hoping to learn new understandings of the connections between people and environment in new ways, in order to understand the interactions of social-cultural-ecological systems under conditions of environmental and climatic change. By understanding the actual and potential impacts of climate change and environmental change, people will be better able to make plans for the future.
